identification.name: Inconel 718 (Precipitation Hardened)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely available as wrought bar, billet, plate, sheet, strip, and ring from aerospace suppliers. Also supplied as gas-atomised spherical powder for metal AM (DMLS/SLM and Binder Jet). AMS (Aerospace Material Specification) 5662 (bar/billet, solution annealed), AMS 5663 (bar, precipitation hardened), AMS 5664 (sheet/strip). UNS (Unified Numbering System) N07718, Werkstoff Nr. 2.4668.
identification.notes: Inconel 718 is a precipitation-hardenable nickel–chromium superalloy. Properties given are for the standard engineering condition: solution annealed (982°C/1 h, air cool) then double-aged (718°C/8 h, furnace cool at 55°C/h to 621°C, hold 8 h, air cool). This treatment precipitates the primary strengthening phase γ″ (Ni₃Nb, body-centred tetragonal) plus secondary γ′ (Ni₃(Al,Ti), FCC (face-centred cubic)), raising yield strength from ~550 MPa (annealed) to >1,000 MPa while retaining useful ductility. Solution-annealed material is preferred when weldability or cold-forming is required; the aged condition is used for structural hardware. Max continuous service temperature is ~650°C; above 700°C the γ″ phase reverts to the stable δ phase (Ni₃Nb, orthorhombic), causing overaging and strength loss. Short-term peak temperature ~980°C. Inconel 718 is the most widely printed superalloy in metal AM (additive manufacturing) (DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering)/SLM (Selective Laser Melting)/LPBF (laser powder bed fusion)); as-built parts contain high residual stresses and are typically stress-relieved, then solution annealed, optionally HIPed (Hot Isostatic Pressing, to close internal porosity), then double-aged to recover mechanical properties approaching wrought. Curie temperature is −112°C; above this the alloy is paramagnetic (magnetically inert at room temperature). Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS (ultimate tensile strength)/√3 = 1240/√3 ≈ 716 MPa. Electrical conductivity derived from resistivity ~1.25 µΩ·m: (ρ_Cu/ρ_IN718) × 100 = (0.01724/1.25) × 100 ≈ 1.4% IACS (International Annealed Copper Standard). Thermal diffusivity is derived from thermal conductivity (k), density (ρ), and specific heat (Cp) — not an independently measured value.

typical_usage: Aerospace turbine discs, blades, combustor liners, fasteners, and casings; rocket engine components; cryogenic tankage hardware; nuclear reactor core components; oil/gas downhole tooling; high-performance racing engine parts. The dominant superalloy for metal AM in aerospace and defence.
